hypothesis: In a species-level molecular phylogeny of mammals, Perissodactyla (represented by Equidae, Rhinocerotidae, Tapiridae) forms a clade with or is sister to Lagomorpha (Leporidae), to the exclusion of other ungulates (Artiodactyla, Cetacea, Proboscidea, Hyracoidea, Sirenia) and of other Rodentia.
pass_criterion: In at least 95% of trees from the Upham et al. 2019 credible tree sets (Data_S7), the Perissodactyla and Leporidae (or Lagomorpha) tips form a clade that excludes all Artiodactyla and all non-lagomorph Rodentia. That means Perissodactyla+Lagomorpha is monophyletic and the Perissodactyla-Leporidae patristic distance is smaller than both the Perissodactyla-Artiodactyla and the Leporidae-Rodentia mean patristic distances.
fail_criterion: In fewer than 5% of sampled trees is Perissodactyla+Lagomorpha a clade excluding Artiodactyla and Rodentia. Equivalently, the Perissodactyla-Artiodactyla patristic distance is smaller than the Perissodactyla-Leporidae distance, or the Leporidae-Rodentia distance is smaller than the Leporidae-Perissodactyla distance, in more than 50% of trees. Results between these bounds count as inconclusive and the claim is not confirmed.
interpretation: Thompson's "more closely related" is read as phylogenetic recency of common ancestry. It is measured as clade membership and patristic (time-calibrated) distance on a modern molecular tree, not as similarity of skull form. His inference came from a uniform flexure transformation of the skull, which is a morphological argument. The test therefore checks the phylogenetic conclusion only. In the modern tree, Perissodactyla sits in Laurasiatheria, while Lagomorpha sits with Rodentia in Glires within Euarchontoglires. Perissodactyla is expected to be closest to Artiodactyla and relatives (Cetartiodactyla, Carnivora, Pholidota, Chiroptera), and Lagomorpha closest to Rodentia. "Other ungulates" is operationalised as Artiodactyla, with Proboscidea, Hyracoidea and Sirenia as a sensitivity check. "Rest of the Rodentia" is operationalised as the order Rodentia in the modern sense.

dataset.name: Inferring the mammal tree: Species-level sets of phylogenies for questions in ecology, evolution, and conservation
dataset.why_it_fits: It provides time-calibrated species-level mammal trees. Data_S7_Mammalia_credibleTreeSets_tipDR.zip holds sets of posterior trees, and Data_S1 holds the master taxonomy mapping species to order and family. Fields used: tip labels, taxonomy (order, family), and branch lengths. These give the Perissodactyla, Leporidae, Artiodactyla and Rodentia tips, from which monophyly and patristic distances can be computed across trees.
